claims.statement: Verstappen won the 2016 Spanish Grand Prix on his first race appearance for Red Bull. Formula 1’s report describes the victory as his first in the championship.

evidence.locator: Opening race report: first Red Bull race, maiden victory ahead of Räikkönen

claims.statement: The 2016 classification lists Verstappen with Toro Rosso Ferrari through the Russian round, then Red Bull Racing TAG Heuer from Spain. These are recorded constructor labels, not evidence of contractual terms or legal succession.

evidence.locator: Team column: opening four rounds Toro Rosso Ferrari; Spain onward Red Bull Racing TAG Heuer

claims.statement: The Spanish result row records first place on 15 May 2016; the same season’s Brazilian row records third place on 13 November. They offer two distinct race records to explore, not a complete account of how either race unfolded.

evidence.locator: Spain 15 May P1 and Brazil 13 November P3 rows

claims.statement: In the official final 2021 drivers’ table, Verstappen leads with 395.5 points and Hamilton follows with 387.5. This classification supports the title outcome; explaining the final-race controversy requires separate evidence.

The official 2023 drivers’ standings list Verstappen first with 575 points and Sergio Perez second with 285, both under Red Bull Racing Honda RBPT. These totals include championship scoring and must not be reconstructed from race-only rows.
The final 2024 table places Verstappen first with 437 points and Lando Norris second with 374. The statement is bounded to 2024; it makes no claim about titles in later seasons.
